findings.claim: Referenced-assembly types are normally skipped by TypeCollector, so no formatter is generated for them. The new GeneratedFormatterCollector deliberately bypasses that skip for types named in [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]. This is an explicit opt-in and consistent with the requirement and the ledger.

receipt_plan.detail: [L15] Types from referenced assemblies get no formatter from the compiling assembly by default, so the absence of automatic generation is not a defect. The opt-in attribute path in GeneratedFormatterCollector does not contradict it.

findings.claim: The surrogate design plus the contractless default was not settled in the thread, but the ledger answers the intent question: follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: [L23] Contractless by default plus an optional SurrogateType is accepted; [L24] read-only members are skipped as the change does.

findings.claim: An unrelated edit to MessagePackPrimitives.Writers.cs changes the timestamp encoding check from `0xffffffff00000000` to `0x00000000ffffffff`. This inverts which values use the 6-byte timestamp32 format. It falls outside the feature's scope and affects wire bytes for every user, and numeric serialization is bug-prone per [L16].

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize DateTime values with whole seconds (nanoseconds 0) and with nonzero nanoseconds on base and head builds; compare bytes. Base produces timestamp32 (6 bytes) for zero-nanosecond values and head does not.

findings.claim: The new MsgPack019-022 diagnostics are reported only from the generator's RegisterSourceOutput, not from the analyzer. The MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer registers the descriptors but has no code that reports them. The doc pages describe them as analyzer diagnostics.

receipt_plan.detail: Search MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.Initialize for GeneratedMessagePackFormatter handling; none is present, so diagnostics appear only when the generator runs.
